nodes.label: DEPENDENCY_FIX.md
nodes.rationale: Switched from Coqui TTS to gTTS due to numpy version conflicts. Trade-off: requires internet, slightly higher latency, less voice control. Offline alternative: pyttsx3.

nodes.label: Horus Platform
nodes.rationale: AI-powered aviation training platform with real-time ATC voice communication, role-routed frontend apps, and strict multi-tenant boundaries.

nodes.label: Voice Communication Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Pilot Audio (WebSocket) -> Speech-to-Text (Whisper) -> ATC Agent (LangChain + Ollama) -> Text-to-Speech (gTTS) -> Radio Effects (scipy filters) -> ATC Audio Response (WebSocket).

nodes.label: Multi-Tenant Architecture
nodes.rationale: Strict organization-scoped APIs with role-based access controls. Data ownership mapped via org_id columns and seat-based membership.

nodes.label: Role-Routed Frontend
nodes.rationale: Three Nuxt apps: Hangar (student), Tower (org admin/instructor), Squawk (platform admin).

nodes.label: Seat-Based RBAC
nodes.rationale: Users are associated with organizations via seats table with roles: admin, instructor, student. Platform-admins bypass seat checks.

nodes.label: Keycloak Authentication
nodes.rationale: OIDC/JWT-based auth with realm 'horus'. Two clients: horus-web (public, PKCE) and horus-api (bearer-only). Token lifespan 300s, session idle 1800s.

nodes.label: Google Text-to-Speech (gTTS)
nodes.rationale: Primary TTS engine chosen after Coqui TTS dependency conflicts. Requires internet. Supports 100+ languages.

nodes.label: Coqui TTS
nodes.rationale: Originally planned TTS engine. Abandoned due to strict numpy version conflicts. Could be restored in isolated Python 3.10 environment.

nodes.label: Multi-Language Support
nodes.rationale: English and Spanish supported for STT (Whisper auto-detect), TTS (gTTS dynamic response), and LLM prompts (language-specific ICAO phraseology).

nodes.label: ICAO Phraseology
nodes.rationale: Standard aviation communication terminology used in both English and Spanish (OACI) for ATC agent prompts.

nodes.label: Application Settings
nodes.rationale: JWT issuer validation is strict in production (single issuer) but accepts local aliases in development/testing to allow easy switching between direct URLs and Traefik-hosted URLs.

nodes.label: Organization Scoping Pattern
nodes.rationale: Platform admins can access any organization. Other users can only access their own organization as declared in the JWT. This is a cross-cutting concern applied consistently across API routes.

nodes.label: Fallback Graceful Degradation Pattern
nodes.rationale: When AI/LLM services are unavailable, the system falls back to basic structural checks or stub data. Applied in flight plan text/image parsing and validation, and in session scoring.

nodes.label: Session Replay Normalization
nodes.rationale: Complex normalization logic transforms raw track points, flight insights, and voice logs into a unified replay payload for frontend rendering. Includes timestamp alignment and severity mapping.

nodes.label: Badge Criteria Evaluation Engine
nodes.rationale: Simplified rule engine that evaluates badge criteria JSONB against student stats. Supports flight_hours, maneuvers, scenarios, assessments, streak, and score threshold rules.

nodes.label: Redis Cache with DB Fallback Pattern
Catch-All Error Middleware for CORS Safety
Sentinel Object Pattern for Platform Admins
TrainingModule ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Modules can be organisation-scoped (org_id set) or global/platform-level (org_id IS NULL). Contains ordered scenarios via module_scenarios association table.

nodes.label: TrainingSession ORM Model
nodes.rationale: client_id kept for backward compatibility; nullable for new user-based sessions.

nodes.label: TrainingSessionEvent ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Audit event emitted during training session lifecycle transitions.

nodes.label: User ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Application user linked to a Keycloak identity. Each user has a globally-unique UUID primary key and a Keycloak subject identifier.

nodes.label: UserPreferences ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Per-user preferences stored as a JSONB document. Each user has at most one preferences row enforced by unique constraint on user_id.

nodes.label: Waypoint ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Navigation waypoint, airport, or radio-navigation aid. The type column distinguishes between waypoints, airports, VORs, NDBs, fixes, and intersections.

nodes.label: ScenarioWaypoint ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Ordered association between a scenario and its waypoints. sequence_order defines route order; optional altitude and speed constraints encode approach/departure restrictions.

nodes.label: SessionTrack ORM Model
nodes.rationale: Recorded flight track for session replay. Stores complete trajectory as JSONB array of track points.

nodes.label: FlightInsight ORM Model
nodes.rationale: AI-generated insight for a training session. Flags deviations, performance highlights, communication issues, or procedural notes at a specific point in session timeline.

nodes.label: OrganizationWithStats Schema
nodes.rationale: Extends basic organization fields with live counts for seats, active sessions, and scenarios.

nodes.label: SeatWithUser Schema
nodes.rationale: Seat enriched with associated user details to render member list without extra round-trips.

nodes.label: UserWithSeats Schema
nodes.rationale: User details with organization memberships (seats).

nodes.label: AdminStats Schema
nodes.rationale: Platform-wide statistics for admin dashboard.

nodes.label: AnalyticsOverview Schema
nodes.rationale: Organization-level analytics with aggregate counters, 30-day time series, and popular scenarios.

nodes.label: LeaderboardEntry Schema
nodes.rationale: Users ranked by completed training sessions with voice-log statistics.

nodes.label: ContentCategoryDetailRead Schema
nodes.rationale: Category with nested articles for detail endpoint.

nodes.label: ContentCategoryRead Schema
nodes.rationale: Hierarchical category with nested children.

nodes.label: FlightPlanFromText Schema
nodes.rationale: Schema for creating flight plan from free-text input.

nodes.label: FlightPlanFromImage Schema
nodes.rationale: Schema for creating flight plan from image upload via OCR.

nodes.label: TrainingModuleWithScenarios Schema
nodes.rationale: Training module with associated scenarios eagerly loaded.

nodes.label: TrainingSessionReplayResponse Schema
nodes.rationale: Aggregated payload for session replay endpoint including track, insights, voice logs, and scoring.

nodes.label: SessionCompletionScoring Schema
nodes.rationale: Normalized scoring block after completing a session.

nodes.label: PreferencesData Schema
nodes.rationale: Full typed preference structure documenting canonical shape and providing sensible defaults for JSONB column.

nodes.label: HorusState
nodes.rationale: All agents in the orchestrator share a single HorusState TypedDict that flows through the graph. Sub-states are nested TypedDicts so each agent can read/write only the slice it owns while the orchestrator keeps everything in one place.

nodes.label: check_airspace
nodes.rationale: In production this would query an FAA NASR / EuroControl database or a vector-tile service. For the MVP we provide realistic mock data for the major US Class-B airports used in training scenarios.

nodes.label: calculate_fuel_burn
nodes.rationale: Default fuel-burn rates are training-grade approximations, not ops manuals.

nodes.label: fetch_metar
nodes.rationale: In production these would call the Aviation Weather Center API (aviationweather.gov) or a DATIS feed. For the MVP we return realistic but static mock data for major US airports.

nodes.label: fetch_taf
nodes.rationale: In production these would call the Aviation Weather Center API (aviationweather.gov) or a DATIS feed. For the MVP we return realistic but static mock data for major US airports.

nodes.label: Seed script
nodes.rationale: Populates the database with realistic aviation training data for local development. The script is idempotent — it checks for existing rows before inserting and can safely be run multiple times.

nodes.label: Mock AsyncSession Pattern for Unit Tests
JWKS Key Rotation with Cache Refresh
Monorepo Structure Decision
nodes.rationale: Single monorepo with independently deployable units. Root contains shared tooling; each subdirectory is fully self-contained with own dependencies and deployment targets.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL 16 with SQLAlchemy Async
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL 16 via SQLAlchemy 2.x async with Alembic migrations. Chosen because aviation training data is highly relational, AsyncPG provides excellent async performance for FastAPI, and Alembic provides safe version-controlled schema migrations.

nodes.label: Deployment to Cloudflare Pages and VPS
nodes.rationale: Frontend deployed to Cloudflare Pages for edge CDN; backend deployed to private VPS via Docker Compose. Independent deployments that communicate over HTTPS/WSS.

nodes.label: Flight Plan Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Multi-source flight plan pipeline with three input methods (form, text, image/OCR), shared parse/normalize step, AI-powered validation via LangGraph validation graph, and explicit lifecycle states (draft, validated, active, completed, rejected).

nodes.label: Module-Level State Pattern
nodes.rationale: Module-level refs are used as singletons shared across all component instances that call the composable. This avoids prop-drilling and ensures consistent state. Actions are registered lazily on mount to allow each page/component to wire up its own callbacks without global coupling.

nodes.label: localStorage Persistence Pattern
nodes.rationale: Keyboard shortcuts and user preferences are persisted to localStorage with try/catch guards for corrupt data or quota exceeded. This provides immediate availability on page load while backend sync happens asynchronously in the background.

nodes.label: Backend Sync with Local Cache Fallback
nodes.rationale: Preferences load from localStorage first for instant UI response, then fetch from backend and merge. Deep merge preserves nested structures. The pattern ensures offline resilience: even if backend is unreachable, user settings are available.

nodes.label: WebSocket-Based Real-Time Voice Communication
nodes.rationale: Voice communication uses WebSocket for bidirectional real-time audio streaming. Audio is recorded via MediaRecorder (WebM/Opus), sent as ArrayBuffer, and received as Blob for playback. JWT token is passed as a query parameter for authentication.

nodes.label: Role-Based Access Control Middleware
nodes.rationale: Middleware enforces role-based access control using hasAnyRole from useAuth. Auth middleware runs first to ensure authentication, then admin/instructor middleware checks specific roles. Unauthenticated users are redirected to login with a redirect parameter.

nodes.label: Microservice URL Configuration
nodes.rationale: The frontend integrates with three backend microservices: Hangar (scenarios/content), Tower (ATC/voice), and Squawk (auth). URLs are injected via runtime config from environment variables with localhost defaults for development. Cloudflare Pages preset is used for production deployment.

nodes.label: Dark Theme Aviation Design System
nodes.rationale: The design system uses a dark aviation-themed palette with cyan accents (#00d4ff), semantic status colors (success/warning/danger/info), and JetBrains Mono for monospace. Glow effects, grid patterns, and animations create a cockpit-like aesthetic.

nodes.label: Responsive Three-Pane Layout Pattern
nodes.rationale: Default and mission layouts implement a responsive three-pane layout: nav sidebar (left), main content (center), and detail panel (right). On mobile (<1024px), sidebars become overlays with backdrop dimming and mutual exclusivity (opening one closes the other). Desktop nav state is persisted to localStorage.

nodes.label: Session Replay Playback Architecture
nodes.rationale: Session replay fetches both session details and audit events in parallel. Playback uses setInterval with configurable speed multipliers (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x). Computed properties filter insights and voice logs to show only those at or before the current playback index, creating a synchronized replay experience.

nodes.label: API Response Transformer Pattern
nodes.rationale: useStats uses dedicated transformer functions (toStudentStats, toFlightHourLog, etc.) to map snake_case API responses to camelCase frontend types. This decouples the API contract from the UI data model and allows handling of optional/nullable fields with sensible defaults.
